You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | S&P Earnings Growth Hits 30-Year High; NVIDIA Discloses SpaceX Stake, Becomes Sixth-Largest Shareholder (August 17, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot Topics
Federal Reserve Dynamics Strong earnings support the market, while high interest rates put valuation pressure on AI capital expenditures.
S&P 500 Q2 earnings grew 31% year-over-year, significantly exceeding Wall Street’s prior 23% expectation — the strongest growth rate since 1992 after excluding major recessions.
Over 90% of constituents have reported; first-half earnings are on track for the best performance since 2021.
Markets are reassessing the impact of rising long-term rates on high-valuation tech stocks. AI projects have long payback periods, and higher rates reduce the present value of future cash flows.
Market Impact : Earnings growth has completed a relatively healthy valuation reset, with the P/E ratio falling from around 26x at the start of the year to below 22x. The short-term “earnings bull” narrative dominates, but the sustainability of massive AI capital spending under high rates remains a focus.
International Commodities Hormuz risks unresolved; oil prices stabilize at elevated levels.
Brent crude held steady below $89, up about 6% last week; WTI hovered near $83.
Israel intensified strikes on Hezbollah in Lebanon, another vessel was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, and U.S.-Iran talks remain stalled.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent indicated new restrictive measures on Iran could be announced as early as this week; Middle East oil exporters’ volumes remain above market expectations.
Market Impact : Geopolitical risk premium supports high oil prices in a range-bound pattern. Supply-chain uncertainty has prompted Indian refiners to lock in forward crude early. Short-term oil volatility remains highly dependent on U.S.-Iran negotiations and Strait transit developments.
Macro Policy Trump directs sharp reduction in U.S.-South Korea joint military exercises; AI data-center demand spills over into power generation and energy storage.
Trump stated he has instructed the Department of Defense to significantly scale back joint exercises with South Korea, calling them “extremely costly” and sending the wrong signal to North Korea.
AI data-center construction has become a new engine for U.S. manufacturing. Caterpillar, Cummins , Eaton , and Ford are all expanding power generation, distribution, and energy-storage capacity.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rare publicly stated that AI must win public trust through verifiable scientific breakthroughs (such as curing cancer).
Market Impact : Reduced military exercises send a signal of easing toward North Korea. Data-center demand spillover directly benefits power-generation and energy-storage equipment makers; the AI commercialization narrative is shifting from “investment” to “delivery.”
II. Market Recap
Commodities & FX Performance
Spot gold : ~$4,405/oz, +0.75%
Spot silver : ~$65.8/oz, +1.84%
WTI crude: ~$81.4/bbl, –0.15%
Brent crude: ~$84.1/bbl, –0.24%
U.S. Dollar Index (DXY): ~99.53, –0.10%
Driver Analysis : Hormuz risks remain unresolved, keeping oil prices elevated and range-bound (Brent rose ~6% last week). Gold traded between geopolitical safe-haven demand and dollar movements, remaining relatively steady. The asset linkage is: prolonged geopolitical stalemate → oil support → inflation concerns not fully dissipated, while strong corporate earnings provide a buffer for risk assets. Short-term commodity volatility will continue to center on U.S.-Iran talks and potential new Iran restrictions this week.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$63,100, +0.06%
ETH : ~$1,890, +0.54%
Total crypto market cap: ~$2.22 trillion, –0.3%
Liquidations (24h): Total $78 million, of which long liquidations $51 million
Bitget BTC/ USDT Liquidation Map: BTC currently ~$63,065. Dense long liquidations clustered below in the $62,400–$62,700 zone; a break below $62,500 could trigger cascading long liquidations. Short liquidations concentrated above in the $63,400–$64,000 area; a breakout above $63,500 could squeeze shorts and push prices higher.
Driver Analysis : Weekend trading was light; the crypto market overall remained in a narrow range. BTC held above $62,000 and ETH stayed relatively stable. Leverage liquidation volumes dropped sharply, indicating cautious sen time nt. On the macro side, strong earnings and high-rate pressure on AI valuations offset each other. In the near term, crypto is likely to continue range-bound consolidation, with attention on upcoming FOMC minutes and regulatory developments.
U.S. Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones: Closed at 53,732.41 (–0.20%), modestly lower
S&P 500: Closed at 7,265.76 (–0.17%), pulled back from highs
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,729.16 (–0.28%), tech under pressure
Tech Giants
NVDA : $225.16 (–0.06%)
AAPL : $305.93 (+0.22%)
MSFT : $495.40 (–0.30%)
GOOGL : $345.90 (–0.13%)
AMZN : $262.65 (–0.94%)
META : $589.85 (–0.86%)
TSLA : $342.27 (+0.68%)
[...]
Performance Summary & Drivers : U.S. equities closed modestly lower on Friday, with all three major indices slightly down. Most tech giants weakened; Amazon and Meta declined more noticeably, while Tesla and Apple showed relative resilience. Markets weighed strong earnings support against high-rate valuation pressure on AI capital spending. The memory and optical communications sectors were active; SanDisk rose over 35% on the week, indicating continued rotation within the AI infrastructure chain.
[...]
2. NVIDIA (NVDA) – First Disclosure of SpaceX Stake Event Overview : NVIDIA disclosed for the first time that it holds SpaceX shares, becoming the sixth-largest shareholder. The stock edged down ~0.06% on Friday. Market Interpretation : This further strengthens NVIDIA’s positioning in the AI infrastructure ecosystem. SpaceX, as a satellite-internet and potential AI-compute-related asset, is viewed by the market as an extension of NVIDIA’s strategic layout. Short-term price impact from overall tech sentiment was limited. Investment Implication : Long-term AI compute and ecosystem synergy logic is reinforced; monitor subsequent stake changes and SpaceX business progress.
[...]
NVIDIA disclosed its SpaceX stake for the first time, becoming the sixth-largest shareholder and reinforcing its AI ecosystem positioning.
[...]
Institutional Views Analysts generally believe that S&P 500 earnings growth hitting a 30-year high shows AI penetration and economic resilience are translating into actual profits; the “earnings bull” narrative dominates in the short term. AI infrastructure spending is beginning to spill over from chips into power generation, energy storage, and related segments, giving equipment makers a new growth curve. NVIDIA’s SpaceX disclosure further strengthens its ecosystem positioning. However, the valuation test of massive AI capital spending under high rates remains; markets must continue verifying investment returns. The overall consensus is that earnings delivery is the current main theme, while geopolitics and interest rates remain the primary disturbance factors.
